sources.title: הגרף הזה סימן תחתית 7 פעמים מאז 2020. ועכשיו? (Did this graph signal a bottom?)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)
principles: When only about a fifth of S&P 500 members trade above their 50-day average, breadth is washed out. Since 2020 such readings often sat near bottoms, but real crises pushed it far lower, so treat it as a setup to confirm, not a buy signal.
An index near its high while most of its members sit below their averages means leadership is narrow. Narrow leadership is fragile and deserves lower conviction on broad bullish calls.
Earnings reactions follow guidance more than the beat. A profit beat paired with weak forward guidance can still sell off hard, so judge a report by what management expects next.
A fear reading on a sentiment gauge is context, not a trigger. Lean contrarian only when breadth, trend and sentiment line up, and say which one would prove the call wrong.
A sector jump on a geopolitical shock, such as energy on shipping-lane tension, says little about the wider market and tends to fade when the headline does.

observations.text: About 20% of S&P 500 members were above their 50-day average, the zone that preceded several rebounds since 2020.
Fear and Greed index read 28 (fear). The S&P 500 printed a doji on 1 Oct and sat about 2% below its all-time high.
Nike fell about 5.7% after earnings: profit beat, but weak forward guidance.
Accenture rose about 15% and Micron about 3% after profit beats.
Alphabet slipped about 1.7% and was described as still inside a technical triangle.
Synopsys reportedly signed a chip development agreement with OpenAI.
Rocket Lab reportedly won a 20-launch contract but was meeting resistance at its 150-day average.
Nu Holdings denied rumours that it would acquire a UK digital bank.
Energy rose about 2% on geopolitical tension around the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: אפוקליפסת הריטל? הסוכן של מטא שמאיים על אמזון (Retail apocalypse: Meta's agent threatening Amazon)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)
principles: When software agents do the shopping, sponsored placements lose their audience. Revenue that depends on a human browsing a page is exposed to any shift toward agent-made purchases.
Agent-era screen, part one: does revenue rely on customers forgetting to cancel, or on friction that stops them switching? An agent that audits subscriptions and compares offers removes both.
Agent-era screen, part two: does profit hinge on paid placement, or is the business only a middleman between buyer and seller? Agents route around both and go straight to the supplier.
In a platform shift, the rails tend to win: whoever settles the payment or runs the compute gets paid whichever agent wins. Prefer picks-and-shovels exposure while the winner is unclear.
Early in a shift, people using AI to help them shop far outnumber agents actually completing purchases. Size a disruption thesis to measured adoption, not to the narrative.

observations.text: Meta's shopping agent was reported at the top of the App Store, with Amazon said to be blocking it. Amazon ad revenue cited at about 68.6B dollars a year.
Cited Morgan Stanley figures: about 5% of purchases made by AI agents, 42% of users using AI to help them shop, and a 20% chance agents dominate online retail by 2030.
Named as likely winners of the agent era: Meta, card networks, Shopify, Walmart, PayPal and compute or chip suppliers.
Named as at risk in the agent era: travel aggregators, subscription gyms, news subscriptions and telecoms.

sources.title: איך לעשות פי 12 תשואה בבורסה בצורה פשוטה - האם זה אפשרי? (A 12x market-return strategy?)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)
principles: Buying last year's single best performer looks spectacular in a backtest, but the edge comes from a handful of outlier years. Most years are average or worse, so the result is closer to luck than to a repeatable rule.
A strategy that beats the index in only about three years of five carries heavy psychological cost. Most people abandon it in the losing stretch, which is when it matters.
Turnover and taxes can erase a backtested edge. Yearly rotation that wins before tax can lose to the index after tax, while buying and holding lets compounding do the work.
A concentrated bet on one name is a lottery ticket, not a core holding. Judge any momentum rule by its median year, not its best one.

sources.title: 7 מניות, אותו גרף בדיוק: סוד מטריד לפני שבוע הדיווחים (7 stocks, the same chart before earnings)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)
principles: When unrelated stocks trace the same chart, a shared factor such as rates, risk appetite or retail flows is driving them, not company news. Treat them as one bet and expect them to break together.
The options-implied move is the bar for an earnings reaction. A result is only news if the stock moves beyond what was already priced in.
A stock that ran hard into its report has front-run the good news. It needs a beat plus better guidance just to hold, and a plain beat can still trigger selling.
For each name, know the one segment metric the market is watching, such as a customer mix or a payments volume line. That line moves the stock more than the headline beat.
A breakout from a long range sets a technical target, but the story has to keep up. Without fundamental confirmation, breakouts tend to fail back into the range.

observations.text: Six unrelated growth names were described as tracing the same chart pattern into earnings.
AMD and Arm shared a pattern: consolidation, breakout around 1 Apr, then a steep climb. AMD was cited up about 83% since then.

Palantir: implied move about 11%, revenue estimate about 1B dollars (+73% YoY), EPS estimate 0.29. The commercial vs government mix was the key line. A large short by a well-known investor was reported.
PayPal: implied move about 9.5% after a 31% bounce from February lows. Transaction revenue was cited up about 4% and Venmo about 20%. A turnaround under the new CEO was the test.
AMD: revenue growth estimate about 30%. It had to show AI inference demand in data center and client to justify the premium.
Uber had broken its downtrend line and retested support. A strong EPS beat and guidance were needed to confirm the reversal.
Arm: implied move about 14%, revenue estimate +18%. It had broken out of a long 80 to 190 dollar range, with a technical target near 280.
AppLovin had dropped about 19% the prior quarter, was forming a possible head-and-shoulders, and needed to clear resistance near 525.
IonQ: loss-making. The market wanted deployment numbers and updates on a reported 9.7B dollar data-center partnership with Microsoft.

sources.title: רעידת אדמה: 180 דוחות יזיזו את התיק שלכם (180 earnings reports will move your portfolio)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)
principles: A peak earnings week that also holds a central-bank decision piles up event risk. Avoid new high-conviction calls whose horizon spans that week unless the event is the thesis.
For companies that beat every quarter, a beat is already priced. Only the size of the beat or a change in guidance moves the stock.

For mega-cap tech in the AI build-out, capex guidance and cloud growth now move the stock more than EPS. Higher capex can dent near-term EPS without hurting the stock if cloud revenue confirms the spend.
A sleepy chart into earnings usually comes with a small implied move. Such names need a new narrative, not a routine beat, to re-rate.

observations.text: About 180 S&P 500 companies (36% of the index) were reporting in one week alongside a Fed rate decision.
Robinhood: implied move about 10.6%, revenue above 1B dollars. Crypto vs fiat volumes, net interest revenue and prediction markets were the lines to watch.
SoFi: implied move about 11.8%, revenue estimate 1.04 to 1.05B dollars, down about 30% YTD with resistance near 19. Galileo platform growth was the doubted segment.
Alphabet: implied move about 5.9%, revenue estimate about 91B dollars (+20% YoY), EPS 2.63. Cloud growth, YouTube ads and capex mix (own chips vs Nvidia) were key.
Microsoft: implied move about 7%, revenue estimate about 81B dollars, chart weak vs peers. Azure growth, paid Copilot adoption and OpenAI terms were the swing factors.
Meta: implied move about 8%, revenue estimate about 55B dollars, EPS 6.71. A workforce cut was rumoured; capex guidance, Llama traction and Reality Labs burn were key.
Amazon: implied move about 6%, revenue estimate about 177B dollars, near all-time highs. AWS growth was the driver; retail margins were secondary.
Apple: implied move about 3%, revenue estimate about 109B dollars. Only an on-device AI timeline or news on a reported CEO transition was expected to move it.
